answer: Let trust propagate through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, with voting weight tied to probability of reaching the trusted core. A sybil cluster may spiral internally, but its sparse external bridge yields low conductance, φ(S)=Q(S,S̄)/π(S). From stationary mass in S, escape within t steps is at most tφ(S); thus the cluster’s reachable aggregate voting weight is bounded by its small cut, not its internal size. A gale of fabricated attestations cannot cheaply raise that bound.
